title: Measured Agent Usage Telemetry: Orchestrator-Queried Before/After Token and Quota Snapshots per Mission, Feeding Evidence-Based Model Assignment
target_platform: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (agy) CLIs and the local MLX server (Copilot only under an explicit human-approved, usage-query-only exception); the evaluating-agent-work skill; the cli-agent skill
hypothesis: A deterministic usage probe run by the orchestrator (not self-reported by the worker model) that snapshots each backend's own usage surfaces at every real mission checkout and checkin, and stores the measured delta with task class, model, wall-clock time, turns, retries and outcome quality in the evaluating-agent-work ledger, yields: (a) measurable per-task token deltas for >= 3 of the 4 backends (claude, codex, agy, local) agreeing within +/-10% with the vendor's own session totals; (b) where a backend exposes quota-window state (5-hour and weekly), a before/after window reading flagged noisy whenever other sessions were active; (c) after >= 12 real measured tasks, a per-task-class predictor whose held-out MAPE on tokens is <= 30% and >= 20% lower than the static per-task ceilings in track_budget.py; (d) a measured effort multiplier per (backend/model, task class): cost, wall-clock time and retry rate relative to a reference model, so that 'cheap per credit' models are not recommended on price alone when they cost several times the time and effort on a task class; and (e) a model-assignment recommendation that weighs expected cost, time, success rate and remaining 5-hour/weekly headroom, and shifts load to a backend with headroom when another is constrained, with zero credentials, auth tokens or prompt contents written to any tracked file. (f) A fuel gauge visible at boot and at checkout flags any backend whose tightest window is under 15% remaining, and a calibrated percent-to-token estimate predicts the next window percent movement within +/-50% once >= 5 non-concurrent percent points of data exist.
falsification_criteria: Fewer than 3 backends yield a measurable per-task delta; any delta deviates > 10% from the vendor-reported session total; the held-out MAPE is > 30% or not >= 20% better than the static estimates; a quota-window reading cannot be attributed (other sessions' usage swamps the mission's own delta) and no mitigation restores attribution; any auth token, API key or prompt text appears in a tracked file or log; the probe reaches Copilot (a corporate account the cli-agent skill marks work-only) without explicit per-run human approval and usage-query-only scope; or obtaining a backend's quota state requires scraping an undocumented private endpoint or violating its terms (then record that backend as unmeasurable, not hacked). If worker self-report proves as accurate as orchestrator measurement, the measured path is not justified and the result is recorded as such. Also falsified if, with >= 12 real tasks, the measured data shows no usable difference in effective cost or time between models within a task class (the effort multiplier is noise), or the recommender's top choice is outperformed on effective cost by a random choice among unconstrained backends on held-out tasks. Also falsified if the calibrated percent-to-token estimate misses subsequent percent movement by more than 50% on >= 3 held-out measurements, or if a backend reaches 0% remaining without the gauge having flagged it LOW beforehand.
phases: P1 Verify and extend discovery (largely pre-answered, so confirm rather than assume): re-run the zero-token probes (`agy -p /usage --output-format json`, `claude -p /usage`) and assert they cost 0 tokens each time; parse them into the common schema; check `codex doctor`, `codex debug` and `codex agents` for a free usage surface, and confirm which codex rollout field is freshest and how stale rate_limits can be; discover whether claude's usage view exposes per-model tokens headlessly or only interactively; probe copilot only under the human-approved exception. Pre-register a per-backend prediction (measurable yes/no, source, cost of the probe) before running.

P2 Build usage_probe.py in evaluating-agent-work: snapshot/diff per backend with a common schema (backend, model, tokens in/out/cached/reasoning, window percents and reset times where available, source, timestamp, concurrent-session flag); read only the named fields (never auth.json or credentials); redaction test; write to a gitignored raw store plus an aggregate committed ledger. (BUILT: usage_probe.py, 74 tests incl. real captured fixtures).

P3 Attribution: separate the mission's own tokens (from its session transcript or headless output, primary signal) from window-percent deltas (secondary, shared with every other session on the account); define the concurrent-activity flag and a minimum-delta rule; validate against synthetic and real runs.

P4 Wire into the mission cycle: the orchestrator (human-run today, MISSION-033's orchestrator later) calls snapshot before dispatch and after completion; extend track_budget.py record to ingest measured deltas with source=measured versus estimated, task class and outcome; the existing score_contribution token-economy dimension reads measured cost when present.

P5 Passive collection during real missions (no synthetic pilot): checkout takes a zero-token snapshot and checkin takes another, recording measured tokens (own-session transcript for claude; vendor output or rollout totals elsewhere), window deltas with a concurrent-activity flag, wall-clock seconds, turns, retries and the outcome quality score into track_budget (source=measured, task class). The mission's verdict is deferred until >= 12 real measured tasks accumulate (the corroboration check runs `usage_probe.py evaluate` and the effort-multiplier report); until then the mission stays PROPOSED/open with the collection live. Copilot is excluded unless the human approves a one-off usage-only read.

P6 Recommender, references and docs: add a `recommend --task-class X` query returning ranked backend/model with expected cost, time, success rate, headroom, evidence counts and confidence, seeded by the price/capability catalog in cli-agent's cheapest_models.md and overridden by measured data as it accumulates, never overriding the human or the fallback-chain rules; write the single-source reference evaluating-agent-work/references/usage-telemetry-sources.md (per-backend surfaces, freshness, hazards), a short operating-sanctuary-guardian reference (backend-headroom-and-usage-snapshots.md: snapshot points in the lease lifecycle, optional boot-digest headroom line, pointer only), update token-budget-profiles.md and cli-agent routing guidance, and give MISSION-033's orchestrator skill a dispatch-budget reference that points here; record the verdict with a per-backend measurability table.

P7 Fuel gauge and cost (added 2026-11-04 at the human's direction: measure efficiency AND know how much fuel is left): boot-briefing Fuel gauge line from a cached snapshot, checkout headroom warnings, percent-to-token calibration and runway estimate (refuses until enough non-concurrent data), dollar cost computed from the cli-agent skill's own model catalog (exact model id only, with cache rates; null when the model is absent, no duplicated price table). BUILT; calibration and cost accuracy await real-mission data. Catalog prerequisite resolved upstream 2026-11-04 (PR #747); codex per-task tokens now automatic.
design_constraints: Measured over self-reported: a model cannot see its own account quota; the orchestrator queries the vendor surfaces deterministically before and after. Worker self-report is recorded only as a comparison arm.
Secret hygiene: never read, copy or log auth files (e.g. ~/.codex/auth.json), API keys or tokens; the probe reads named usage fields only; a test greps the ledger and logs for credential patterns.

Corporate boundary: Copilot is work-only in the cli-agent skill. It is excluded by default; a Copilot usage probe needs explicit per-run human approval, sends no repo or mission content (usage query only), and is dropped if the human declines. Copilot results never feed Sanctuary routing decisions for sovereign research.

Attribution honesty: window percentages are account-wide; any reading taken while another session was active is flagged noisy and excluded from the predictor unless the mission's own token count corroborates it.
Supported interfaces only: no scraping of private endpoints or reverse-engineering of undocumented APIs; a backend with no supported usage surface is recorded as unmeasurable.
Cheap to run: pilot tasks are small and bounded (token_budget declared per task); the pilot must not exhaust the user's weekly windows; stop and report if any window passes 80%.
Single source of truth: extend track_budget.py and score_contribution.py rather than adding a parallel ledger.
Human Gate: the human approves the Copilot exception, the pilot budget, and any change to routing defaults; the recommender only advises.

The probe itself must be free: the claude and agy usage queries are verified 0-token commands and a test asserts it; never probe a backend with a prompt that goes to the model (the codex /status attempt spent 18,369 tokens, so a codex probe reads rollout files, not the model).

Dispatch guard: the recommender must treat a window below a floor (for example agy Gemini weekly at 12% remaining) as a hard constraint when assigning work, and report which backends are currently constrained.

Freshness: a usage source is admissible for before/after deltas only if its staleness is measured and below the mission's duration; delayed or relative-unit dashboards (the codex Usage tab, up to 6 hours late) are recorded as trend context, never as delta sources.

Read-only TUI driving: if a probe must drive an interactive TUI (codex /usage), it navigates only by reading the screen first, sends no digit or Enter that could select an action (model change, reset redemption, billing), aborts on any confirmation dialog, and a test asserts the codex config and credits are unchanged afterwards; prefer a supported non-interactive surface wherever one exists.

Do not rank by price per credit or token alone: record wall-clock time, turns, retries and outcome quality so a cheap model that needs several times the effort is priced at its measured effective cost (human practice: a very cheap-per-credit model can take 10x the time of a stronger one, yet be the right choice for simple tasks or when a window is nearly exhausted).
Load distribution: when a backend's 5-hour or weekly window is under the floor, the recommendation names an alternative with headroom and says why; the human can always override.

Two instruments, not one: efficiency (cost, time, retries per model) AND a fuel gauge (remaining window/credits) that is visible at boot and at checkout. A cheaper-per-unit model is never recommended when its window is under the floor; a gauge nobody sees is not a gauge.

Do not duplicate the cli-agent skill's catalogs: model prices, cache rates, Copilot credit rates and capability tiers are read from its installed *-models.json files; gaps found (e.g. claude-sonnet-5-5 and gpt-6-luna missing, catalog verified 2026-09-09) are reported upstream under Protocol 133, never patched with a local table or a proxy model's price.
baseline_evidence: track_budget.py today holds 221,249 tokens across 6 tasks, all hand-entered estimates (--tokens-est), with no before/after measurement and no quota-window data. Probed 2026-11-04 (human screenshots + headless runs): (1) agy: `agy -p "/usage" [--output-format json]` returns quota groups with weekly and five-hour remaining percent and reset timestamps (Gemini models weekly 12% remaining, Claude and GPT models via agy 50%, Gemini 4 Argon 97%) at 0 tokens (num_turns 0, usage.total_tokens 0); the Gemini weekly window being 12% remaining is already a live dispatch constraint. (2) claude: `claude -p "/usage"` returns current-session (5-hour) and weekly percent used with reset times at total_cost_usd 0; the interactive /usage view adds per-model session tokens and cost (this session: $29.55, sonnet-5-5 4.0k in / 592.9k out / 175.5m cache read / 1.5m cache write); the usage breakdown is approximate and covers this machine only, while the window percentages are account-wide. (3) codex: the interactive Usage view (Plus plan: lifetime tokens 1.9B, token activity heatmap, per-day and per-skill stats, tabs Overview/Usage/Messages/Plugins/Skills/Chats) exists, and its Usage tab (7d/30d, by day and by feature) is labelled relative units, approximate, may be delayed up to 6 hours, with the peak day normalised to 100 (so it is unusable for before/after deltas); no headless command for it was found among `codex --help` subcommands (doctor, debug, agents are candidates to check in P1); rollout files in ~/.codex/sessions carry rate_limits (primary 300-minute, secondary 10080-minute used_percent) and total_token_usage; `/status` is NOT a slash command under `codex exec` (it was sent to the model and cost 18,369 tokens), so codex must be read from rollouts, and this install currently fails to spawn its code-mode host (missing codex-code-mode-host binary), a separate defect. (4) copilot: exposes --usage-output-file; its billing command was not reachable non-interactively; unprobed and gated. (5) local MLX: the response usage field; no quota. The mission-cycle model_routing field is still a static judgment with no measured cost-per-task-class behind it. Interactive-TUI findings 2026-11-04: codex `/usage` opens a menu (View analytics, Redeem reset) and `codex` can be driven over a pty with no tmux, but the menus use digit keys as selections, so blind keystrokes can trigger state changes (a blind '2','3' sequence reached the 'Use this reset?' confirmation, backed out unconfirmed); codex also holds consumable free usage-limit resets (3 available, expiring 6 Nov, 30 Nov, 1 Dec) that are themselves a budget resource. Copilot's Current tab shows plan usage in AI credits (AIC: 2,388 / 6,000, 39% used) and a per-session AIC counter, and `copilot --usage-output-file` writes final usage JSON. Codex /usage > View analytics (read-only, screen-guarded) tab 6 Chats lists per-chat Weekly % and 5-hour % of the limit (estimates, 'may exceed 100%', recent activity may be delayed; e.g. one chat 30.3% weekly / 193.9% 5-hour), i.e. a per-task attribution signal that complements window snapshots; Messages tab (per model) and Skills tab report 'Updated Nov 3 11:35 PM UTC', confirming staleness of the dashboard views. Full per-backend table, commands, costs and hazards: LEARNING/experiments/mission-035/research-notes.md. Human practice (2026-11-04): the partner periodically checks real model costs per CLI, researches cheapest models per credit and their capabilities, notes that a very cheap-per-credit model can take ~10x the time/effort of a stronger one on the same output but is right for simple tasks, and checks 5-hour and weekly windows to shift work between CLIs; this mission automates that routine with measured data. Catalog check 2026-11-04: the cli-agent catalogs (verified 2026-09-09) hold per-model prices and capability tiers but lack claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5 and gpt-6-luna (the IDs in use here); pricing the real session with the sonnet-5 stand-in overestimated cost by 52% ($44.79 vs $29.55 reported), so costs for absent models stay null. Resolution 2026-11-04: the cli-agent catalogs were refreshed upstream (companion repo PR #747: Claude 5.5 family, GPT-6 family, Gemini 4 Argon; select_model null-price fix) and installed globally; usage_probe now prices claude-sonnet-5-5 sessions exactly ($29.49 computed vs $29.55 reported, including the 1-hour cache-write rate), and codex per-task tokens are measured automatically from rollout files. Remaining unmeasured: agy per-task tokens (pass --tokens), Copilot.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: P3 attribution design and P6 recommender statistics need a frontier model; P1 discovery and P2 plumbing are cheap-tier work. The pilot deliberately spans backends, so its worker assignment follows the experiment design, not cost.

evidence.details: N=14 measured tasks (11 claude, 1 codex, 2 agy). (c) per-class token predictor: held-out MAPE 122.3% vs static 166.2% (limit 30%; relative improvement 26.4% passes the 20% leg). (f) percent-to-token calibration 56,349 tokens/pct; leave-one-out 5 of 8 within +/-50%, 3 misses = the falsification threshold (misses are 1-2 pct tasks where integer rounding alone is 25-50%). (a) met for 3 of 4 backends with exact tokens; (b) partly met; (d) and (e) not testable at this N. Survived: exact tokens, catalog-based cost, fuel gauge, delegation recorder.

lessons_learned: Free-text task classes are too fine for 14 tasks: use a few size buckets.
The claude window percent is an integer: calibrate on tasks that move it by >= 3 points or pool them.
A same-backend delegate shares the account window with its orchestrator: its window delta is unattributable.
Reasoning tokens bill as output: a cheap model's output count can be 8x its visible answer.
